Reviews.174248:
Oh man, what a ride it's been. 

I first saw the trailer for this game back in 2016 and my jaw dropped. It looked so freaking beautiful, I couldn't believe it. The style just clicked with me, so I pre-ordered it. It's the one and only game I have ever pre ordered. 

When it released, I didn't get the backlash this game got. I mean, it wasn't as awesome as it had been advertised, but I knew that. Rarely a game is as good as it looks in the trailers. I didn't expect the game to be anything out of this world, no pun intended. I just wanted a space exploration game that looked like this one did, and for that, the game served me well. 

I played it for about 40 hours. I spent my first 15 hours in the same 3-planet system, familiarizing myself with each one of those planets as if they were home. Then, I jumped the stars and found the Atlas path. This was the moment when it became stale for me. Since I had spent so much time in one system, I already had acomplished a lot without realizing it. When I jumped to other systems I was craving adventure and the unknown, but it was pretty much what I had already seen. I still liked the vistas, colors and weird stupid animals, mind you, I still haven't grown tired of the style this game has, but gameplay-wise.. yeah, it quickly became  a routine of"mine more minerals for better upgrades and then go see the Altas". After I had done this like 10 times I decided the game was over for me. 

I didn't care for new ships and I knew, since I'm familiar with the narrative style this game tries to evoke, that at the center  of the galaxy there would only be a nihilistic answer to existential questions. So yeah, I didn't care and decided the game was over at 40 hours.

For 60$ I was 2/3rds satisfied, but not so much that I would leave a good review of it in Steam. Since Hello Games said they'd be releasing free updates, I decided to wait until I saw how real they were before writting my review. If they didn't release anything, this would have been negative. If they did, well...

The first update they released was called "Foundation" and it introduced base building and Freighters into the game. I decided to see how it was for myself and quickly grew to like it. Freighters I didn't care much about, but base building seemed like something with potential. They introduced new npcs and quests, as well as many new elements into the game which allowed for different kind of biomes and planets.

Overall, I liked this update, but still not so much as to grant them a full positive review. Although cleverly implemented, the quest chain was easily achievable in little time and in the end all bases ended up looking pretty samey, so I eventualy grew bored with it.

And then came the second update, "Pathfinder". This one introduced more stuff for the bases, vehicles, classes for ships and vehicles, the ability to have more than one ship and the truly godsend mode this game needed from day 1: PERMADEATH.

In my opinion, this is the only way this game should be played. It's extremely hard and requires you to be constatly aware of your resources and storage capacity. Everything is slower in this mode and quite harder to achieve, hence making every little achievement a huge sucess. I had built an entire base in "normal mode" previously and didn't feel as rewarded as I felt when I finally built my first container in "permadeath mode". Also, yes, this means that if you die once, all you've accomplished is instantly lost. You only have one chance to make it, so the more you advance in this mode, the higher the stakes. I died like 10 times before I learned how to reach my broken-down ship alive through trial and error.

I realize this is not for everyone, but for me, this is what I needed. This makes it feel like you're in a hostile environment all the time and makes every small decision count. I can't tell you how many times I tried to float over a cliff and clenched my butt as I barely made it to the other side. It's great stuff, seriously, and if you don't like it, I guess you still have the option to take it easy in "normal mode".

So, tl;dr: 

- Did they lie? Yes, they did. Quite a lot actually. I never cared about what they lied about in the first place, so this didn't factor in at all for me.
- Is this game fun? Yes, yes it is.
- Is it flawed? Yes, in many ways.
- Is it the worst game in Steam? No. People love to hate it though.
- Was it overhyped? Oh yes, beyond belief.
- How much should you pay for this? In my opinion, 40 bucks, tops.

**EDIT AFTER ATLAS RISES UPDATE**

So, now you have a "main story", albeit a kind of simple one based on fetching things and jumping from one planet to the next, but at least it gives the meandering some meaning. Not a lot of meaning, mind you, but some.  I very much preferred the vagueness the game had at launch, where there were not sraight answers to anything. Felt more... immersive. This new storyline, while I get the idea behind it, in my opinion strips away originality and immersion in order to provide a more game-like feeling. Some may appreciate it, but I sure didn't. Anyway,  it's not something that bothers me that much since I can just ignore the main story and everything's fine.

Beyond this, there are a lot of other quality of life improvements and mechanichs-oriented changes, like factios, quests and the like. While I appreciate the extra content, again, it's just refurbishing what we already had and giving it another name. Before, you had to gather materials in order to improve your equipement, but now you have to gather materials that you then sell, to then buy a blueprint, to then gather matherials to THEN upgrade your equipment. For some this will mean you now have a purpose, but for me it just feels like being told what to do when I pretty much had figured it out by myself before. No need for the handholding. 

In the end, true. this update introduced a lot of new stuff, much of which was requested by the fans, but on this instance I think the fans were wrong. This game didn't need a storyline nor did it need quests and factions. It was a pulp-inspired sci-fi game where you felt like a minuscule speck in the universe. Now I feel I'm in a game. Good on Hello Games for listening to their fans, but this game deserved better fans.

**EDIT - NEXT UPDATE**

Well, this certainly completed this game's transformation. Its a pretty different game now from what it once was and one I'm willing to bet most people will now be fine with. You have 3rd person-point-of view for you as well as your ship, lots of new enemies and npcs, far more freedom to build anywhere you wish, and, of course, multiplayer. Right now you get to explore the galaxy with a group of friends, which I think is a great feature and good on them for finally delivering what was promised 2 years ago.

We can safely say the game has redeemed itself and is now a perfeclty functional and robust product. If you like survival games, sci-fi or, heck, oversaturated galaxies, this is for you. I still feel kinda nostalgic for what it once was though.

**EDIT - BEYOND UPDATE**

Jesus Christ, I don't even know anymore. There's underwater base building, submarines, co-op with 32 other people,  a 30-hour campaign, tech trees... This game has transformed itself so much... It's really a testament to Hello Games love for their product and confidence in it. People are still trying to talk shit about the game like it's 2016, but in all honesty, there's nothing to talk shit about now. The game is fully functional and offers a distinctive experience filled to the brim with content. People need to accept these guys delivered on their promises and allow NMS to be good.

**EDIT - PRISM UPDATE**

Holy crap, have I been coming back to re-edit this review for over 6 years? I guess so. This game... it never ends...

The game feels stitched together when it comes to the missions and tutorials and now so much is tied into the weird multiplayer station that you cant access most of the game without entering it, and currently the animations and graphics in that place are so intense and poorly optimized that you can't enter it with a GTX 770. So if you got lucky and could afford a card in 2018 before the still ongoing market crash, namely a card with enough memory to handle the insane video ram memory leaks, you got an alright game. But otherwise I would recommend you steer clear.
Update 2: They delivered what they promised, but as to be expected it is currently a complete bug safari, and not in the fun way where you actually get to look at weird procgen insectoid creatures, but rather crashes, NES tier graphics corruptions, unskippable but easily sequence breakable tutorial that will leave you stuck in space with a nonfunctional ship and no equipment or money or anything to repair with if you crash in the middle of the tutorial. Game is as fun and beautiful as ever, however I am personally having issues with CTD's and memory leaks both in RAM and GPU related(otherwise the NES style texture/sprite glitches and corruptions wouldnt happen)

Update: This game has progressed so much since my review in 2017 that words almost don't do it justice. A lot of people thought the game was going to be a "scam" or "garbage" but the developers did exactly what nobody expected of them, they kept quiet and worked on everything that release didn't bring. Every single update has been massive, old school expansion sized updates actually, all free, no paid DLC at all. Multiplayer is actually a part of the game now, albeit in a limited "coop" fashion right now, however they are working on all sorts of cool new things such as fully fledged multiplayer, VR support and apparently even more updates. Only thing I could wish from them was less "monocultural" planets with more diverse biomes, at least as a planet variant.

It's actually not bad, pretty feature packed, addictive, loads of stuff to do and see and hear. Genuinely entertaining experience. I got stuck at finding a resource for one of the terminal dudes at my base so the scientist could move in. Generally a lot of resource scarcity. You will never run out of carbon and iron though. Funnily enough. Starter ship is a god damn gas guzzler and I think ships in general are that, expensive to maintain and low output. Only bad thing is the absolute eyeraep the game turns into at times but that's more at fault of the RNG than anything else. It's cool, go buy it if you like exploratory sandbox bullsheet.

despite all the bad reviews the game has a lot to offer if you like open worlds and space games. The game showed me unique stuff that I have never seen before in a game. I am still hoping for more content but it is enough to have fun quite some time and more than in many other full price titles.

Update 2021: after having a long break from the game until June 2021 I started again from scratch with a new savegame. I played around 60hrs now on that new save and I must say I really enjoy the title now. There are some major flaws still that I really dislike but the whole package is now much rounder and more complete. For example there are actual missions and a story line you can but don't have to follow while you explore which gives you many options to try and improves variety a lot. You can now build bases (which is actually fun for a while), tame and propagate creatures and have them as pets, buy huge freigthers and build your base inside them, build up your own fleet of frigates and send them on missions for nice rewards, build and drive exocrafts for faster movement on planet surfaces, follow distress signals of lost freighters in order to board them and find a lot of good loot and many more things.
Multiplayer is more or less fully working but still doesn't appeal to me much because there is actually not much you can do as a team since resources are not shared and as far as I can see stuff you can do together is quite limited. 
I run the game on highend hardware and in the past I had stutters and FPS drops in many places. This has improved a lot and the game offers now HDR and runs smooth in 4k with FPS much higher than 60 on my RTX 3090 based system. There have definitely been updates towards next gen tech and this is awesome.

What still bothers me though most in this title is the simplicity. Most stuff is reduced to very simple mechanics, there is no real challenge here. For example flying those space ships is pure arcade and a lot of aided control that you cannot disable like auto leveling or height control. There is no manual landing either. I wish the game had more simulation character when it comes to that. 
I also really hate it when you can see stuff spawning infront of your eyes or when the game intentionally places enemies always behind your back. This is just too obvious for example in the pirate missions. 
Also space is full of asteroids that pop up like 1km infront of you. There is more asteroids than void sometimes but you can still see all planets in the far distance. This is fckn unrealistic and so annoying, and only 3 year old kids believe what happens on the screen. Also, whereever you jump out of hyperspeed (pulse drive) a fleet of freighters and frigates spawns like 5-10s later with big sounds like you are a magnet and as if there were like millions of fleets just waiting for you to come by. WHY?
The total variety in life on planets is highly repetetive and resources are kinda evenly spread through the galaxy means you don't really have to go on missions to gather materials because nothing is really rare or difficult to find so far. When you accept a mission and you leave the system where the mission started you can simply reset it and do the same mission in a new system. That is practical but kinda lame too. 

Anyways despite the flaws this game offers a unique experience and is definitely fun for a certain type of player and there is a lot of zen character for a relaxed time. Credit to the devs for still working on the game and not abandoning it like most other studios would probably have done. I will watch progress and will probably come back to the game again and again.

The limited slots for you personal inventory is easy enough to solve by farming the drop pods, which i found in plenty on multiple planets. The real problem is the ship, with worthwhile slot number increases being MASSIVE ammounts of money, your left either repairing crashes, for +1 slot or saving 10's of millions. That being a problem because the economy is broken, there are exploits and tricks to be done. However making the massive cash required for a ship, means you'll never probably buy one. 

Ship flying is AWEFUL. You dont so much fly it as suggest it do something and then it decides if it feels like doing that. It typically doesnt. This leads to a big issue for me with space combat, its aweful, and aggrivating. There are no tactics, its you swarmed by enemies spinning trying to bring terrible weapons to bear. Oh you think you can go over to those large frieghters and they'll fire on the enemies, after all there pirates, they wont. They also appear to often, scanning your ship finding "valuables" everytime, even when your inventory is empty. Its really just a gimmick to make you repair damaged ship modules after you respawn.

I'll only glance over the repetitive mining, and animal scanning to add that there appeal ends after the first star system. They dont pay enough to have them be useful. Outside of resources you need for crafting you'll only harvest Emril, gold, venom sacks, or gravtino balls for decent profit. That "decent" profit will likely cover suit inventory slot upgrades, and a few market purchases for things you havnt learned to craft yet.

You'll just have to go to that white star significantly further away, because reasons. Who knew distance meant nothing with warping? Just another gimmick to tier resources.

I actually do enjoy playing this game, but at this time I cannot recommend the game in good conscience for the following reasons:

Look at the trailers and the screenshots above that are currently advertising this game.

6 out of 11 screenshots are not possible in this game. That's over half.

And while some of the basic gameplay in the trailers remains, they also showcase several things that do not actually exist.

Rhino crashing through the trees? Not possible.

Herd fleeing from a predator as one? Does not exist.

Sandworm deforming terrain as it bursts in and out of the earth? Not possible.

Factions fighting against each other? Does not exist.

Ambient Walker Sentinels? Do not exist.

Wingmen that fly w/ you and attack in unison? Do not exist.

Causing large explosions on the planet w/ ship fire? Does not exist.

The circle portals dotting the landscape in 2nd trailer? Do not exist.

Low-flying directly onto the trading port spacedock? Does not exist.

...and those are just the things that ABSOLUTELY do not exist in this game; I didn't even touch on things that probably don't exist, like the giant snake model or full sand planets, etc that nobody has found at all almost a month after release.

All of that coupled w/ extremely misleading statements by the devs prior to release about many other features that were supposed to be included in the game, and their deafening silence regarding ANY of these missing features post-launch shows a clear lack of respect for their customers.

The game itself can be soothing at times, but it is definitely a niche game.  Once you max out your inventories, there is very little left to do that will hold the average player's attention, and even the game's "story" is all but non-existent.

There is nothing to look forward to, really; just the exact same thing over and over again.

Perhaps at a MUCH lower price point, this would be worth it, but due to devs that you absolutely can NOT trust to do anything that they say (in fact, if Sean Murray says it, I am MUCH less inclined to believe it) and being a barebones bad PS4 port Early Access product masquerading as a finished AAA title, I simply cannot recommend this game to my friends or anyone else at this time.

Update:  Well, it's been several years now since launch and Hello Games, while upsettingly quiet at launch about everything that was missing from their game, have buckled down and tried to make things right.  Perhaps if they had been that quiet from the start, people would not have expected the things that Sean Murray specifically said was in this game.

However, much of the missing content has been added as well as a lot of new stuff that was not teased prior to launch.  This game is finally where it should have been at the start and then some.

It's good.  It was never actually a "bad" game, it just wasn't what was specifically advertised to us.  Now it mostly is.

Reviews.196758:
Latest edit:  Still love this game.  Nearing 1000 hours of playtime and play at least a couple hours every week.
I had an old review on here from launch that I have updated as the game improved.  It went from negative to positive in that time.  

NMS is a combination of every space game ever made, dumbed down to eliminate the crazy amount of options and choices.  I consider this a strong point because there isn't much of a learning curve, and you can jump right into playing.  I'm on PC, so mouse/keyboard is my choice of controls, and it is very simple to fly.  There is no complicated docking or landing, Just press a button to land or enter the docking bay and it is done for you.  I do kind of miss that control sometimes, but then I remember how hard landing was in Elite in 1986 before you could afford a docking computer, and I forget about it.  It allows the player to focus less on which key to press next and lets you enjoy the galaxy around you.  

Gameplay is not overly complex either.  Want a warp drive?  Then you'll need x, y, and z parts.  You will also have to craft those parts and mine for materials.  But wait, some materials require an upgraded mining beam, so you'll need to upgrade that too.  It sounds tedious, and it can be for some people.  But in NMS, it's not the destination, it's the journey.  Just when you have enough mats for that upgrade, you get a blueprint for something cool and you make that instead.  Then you're back to collection mode again, but this time you have the knowledge of where to look.  There are plenty of gameplay reviews and tutorials all over the place so I'll end here.  I enjoy the gameplay a lot!

That said, even though I initially gave it a negative review way back then, I really did enjoy the game for what it was.  However, the minimal gameplay did not justify its $60 cost.  In fact, I tried to return it baxk in 2016  but I spent over 2 hours playing, which is past the terms of Steam's return policy.

Anyway, I kept the game, hoping for a day where it was enjoyable beyond a few hours.  When Atlas Rises was released I tried it out again, and I was hooked.

There were quests and a storyline!  There were things to do and explore.  There were reasons to spend time playing.  There were goals!  It was a real game, finally!

As of this writing I have nearly 300 hours total playing it.  I have done just about everything in the game, and I didn't feel like I was grinding that much.  Farming can be a bit grindy, but once set up it allows you to make enough money for freighters and anything you want, really.  At this point I have all I really need until the NEXT update on Tuesday.  I am currently farming Living Glass, so I have big money for the update.

Speaking of that, I am looking forward to the update, giving me reasons to play again.  

The big question:  Is it still worth $60?  Well, yes and no.  Yes because it is now filled with content and very interesting.  However, it should be less than that since this game is 2 years old now.  

Regardless, you can pick it up on sale all over the place.

So, to wrap up this review:  I love this game now, but didn't at release.  If NEXT lives up to the nauseating amount of hype and you pretend that it just released then it's worth $60 I guess.

My review, after years of waiting for it to actually be release ready, has changed for this game. I can recommend it now. Bugs are minimimal, there is a boatload (or starship load) of content, and it's pretty smooth. I've been having fun, which is what it's all about. 

If games were released in this state, or near it, I'd buy them on release day. But I did make that mistake with this one, and it was the last time I did. I pre-ordered another game recently to try again, because I like being slapped by game companies, I guess. But this game is release ready now, and if you didn't buy it before because it 100% failed to meet the hype set for it before release, it has finally risen to that level of hype. 

Like I said: I'm having fun. My original review is below, everything above this line is new as of July 2021. 

_______________________________

This game has a lot of potential. Unmet potential. 

Let's go into the bugs first.
The frame rate begins to suffer after I've played a while. My machine is a monster compared to the minimum specs for this game, so there is no reason for this other than the program was released in a state of unreadiness. No excuse for that. 

There is an astounding lack of content. Many of the creatures on world A look a lot like the creatures on world B. 

Now lets talk about gameplay. 

The flight model is ludicrously stupid. I should be able to fly my ship into the side of a mountain if I want, or if I make a mistake. Instead the game doesn't let you have anything but marginal control when you're near the ground. This makes landing the ship basically an exercise in luck. Will you get close to where you want to land? Maybe. You do get better at landing in time with practice, but not because you get to look at your landing spot. You simply watch it pass under the nose of your ship, count, and hope you hit the spot you want. This makes landing at trade depots and outposts just stupid. 

I have no idea how to look anything but straight ahead on the PC while flying. Maybe there is a way. If there is, I have yet to figure it out. This stuff should be intuitive. The numerical keypad, for example, would have been a great choice for allowing you to look around in flight. But I guess your head gets locked into place once you're in the ship for your own protection. 

I played a game and with the bonus ship, wound up losing my hyperdrive. After that trying to get a hyperdrive proved futile. I had to start over, which involved going into my computer's SSD and deleting certain files, and then shutting off and restarting steam cloud. WTH? What sort of game doesn't have a "NEW GAME" feature?

So much potential here. So little of it fulfilled.

This all said, I will probably play this game as patches come out, content is added, bugs are patched, and the game gets some actual depth. For now I guess it's back to Rimworld.

[h1]2021 Update:[/h1]
The game has come a long way, the developers have shown amazing passion and dedication in staying with the game even after its fall, it has come back and it is evolving all the time.
A lot of the initial promises have now been implemented into the game and much more.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
The gameplay in No Mans Sky is very simple.
You basically gather resources to craft and recharge various components of your Exosuit, Ship and Multi-Tool.
Gathering resources is done by interaction or by mining objects or killing creatures with your Multi-Tool.
Resources are used to recharge your Exosuit's shields etc which is the 'survival' element of the game.
You also do this to fuel your ship which allows you to visit planets and space stations to upgrade and progress with your journey to the center of the galaxy.
Throughout your journey you will encounter other NPCs in stations or buildings on planets and also in ships which you can interact with to trade, solve puzzles or talk with but will need to unlock words of their language to understand them through accessing objects on the surface of planets.
From what I have played thus far, this is the extent of the core game play.

It is simple but somewhat enjoyable regardless for some reason..

[h1]The Negative:[/h1]
[list]
    [*] [strike]Lots of talk of Multiplayer and being able to find others, but this 'appears' to be lies or deception currently.[/strike]
    [*] Simplistic flight mechanics(One button landing, Auto docking [strike]and Anti-Terrain Collision) in short you cannot    crash.
As such space combat feels clunky..[/strike]
    [*] I have only explored 4 Planets and have already encountered very similar looking flora which makes me wonder how large the asset pool is for the procedural generated content as a whole.
    [*] [strike]Every planet I have visited has had other ships flying around on it and buildings on it and these seem to be the same appearance and layout of every planet.[/strike]
[/list]

[h1]Do I recommend this game?[/h1]
While only a simple game, I am enjoying it thus far so Yes - [b]But[/b] not at its current price level unless it is a game that really appeals to you.
If you are after a space simulator, look toward Elite Dangerous or Star Citizen as this is not a complex game at all.
If you are after an casual/easy going exploration game then this might be what you are looking for.
I recommend looking at more reviews and making your own mind up though as it may not be for everyone.

[h1]Updated for 'Pathfinder Update'[/h1]
I've played the game quite a bit after it's initial launch... So far, the patches haven't really done much for me...

It seems the patches are specifically for people playing with a controller and who are into base-building (which is a feature that didn't fit in Sean's vision of the game, pre-release). I don't like playing first/third person games with a controller, so I play with mouse and keyboard. The controls are TERRIBLE on mouse and keyboard...

Considering mouse/keyboard:
1) Flight controls were okay, but not great to start with and they seem to have been adjusted for the worse... Dogfights were doable, but they're impossible now. Give me Freelancer, Black Prophecy, EVERSPACE kind of controls... The flight controls might be good on a controller, but are terrible with a mouse and keyboard... 
2) They're allowing you to fly lower now, but it's still the same cushion crap that doesn't let you properly control your ship. So if you want decent planetary flight, you still need the user created mod.
3) Still no actual thruster control, no hovering or whatsoever. Just basically 3-gears: slow, medium, fast. And they're automatically selected depending on area (dogfight near space station gets you killed, cause you're limited to slowest flight possible).
4) The quick menu is annoying... Just let me bind all the options in the quick menu to specific keys... 1 key for 1 action, thank you! Right now, it's just another menu that's annoying with too many buttons...

And apart from the controls, the game still isn't that great, considering we were promised rotating planets and an actual simulation style solar system. Planets close to the star would be hot, planets far from the star would be cold. The star is just a pretty picture and the planets do not rotate, nor does their position have any effect on the temperature or ecosystem on the planet.

The game is a massive and repetitive grindfest, and while most survival games are like that, in this case, the base game non-survival mode is like that and the survival-mode is actually more of a grind than ARK.

All the promised content that was lacking at the start, is still lacking and what they have added in the past 8 months is crap that they said wouldn't even be in the game. I didn't want base-building, I wanted a fullfilling exploration game. Instead I get a massive grind with only 6 kinds of planets and base-building... Why?!

So, what do I like about the game?
Well, the graphics are great. I really like the artstyle.
And er... yeah, the potential. It's got that. Whether we'll ever get the features Sean bragged about (rotating planets, massive space battles, warring factions, reputation system that matters, more randomized planets instead of the 6 arch types with only differences in shape of the mountains) I don't know...

[h1]Review updated for 'Foundation Update'[/h1]
In short, I still can't recommend this game, read on for my experience with the new update.

After 2 minutes of loading, I finally got into my survival game. Now, bear in mind, I played this game for 100 hours and knew what I was doing, yet I died 3 times in like 30 minutes because of the random nature and the unbalanced systems in survival mode.

Basically, you need to do several things to survive:
1) Get plutonium and carbon (used to be either was good enough, but not anymore) to keep life support up, without it, you suffocate.
2) Get iron and platinum, or zinc, to keep your shield up, without it, you die from the environment.
3) Get to safety / shelter / ship.

I spawned on a radioactive planet, so the environment was killing me. Will need regular shelter or a lot of zinc and or iron and platinum to keep my shield up.
Then there was no plutonium in my immediate region, so I couldn't craft energy to keep life support up.
These 2 facts, meant that just by spawning, I was already doomed to die a slow death. The only chance at survival I had, was pick a direction and get lucky. I didn't get lucky. I, eventually, found a cave, filled with iron and no plutonium, or platinum for that matter. They used to be filled with plutonium, this one wasn't.

On top of that, scanner cooldown has been increased by a ton, meaning it takes a lot longer to find the right direction for your required materials. 
The mining laser cooldown has been increased too, although a minor problem, add this to the already quickly declining energy levels of life support, shield and the mining laser energy itself, means it's a lot harder to get the required materials to keep yourself alive.

So, basically, all that survival seems to be doing, is just make it impossible to survive if you're unlucky with your starting planet, and on top of that, make it even slower to progress before eventually, the game might actually still become too easy.

The idea is great, but as with anything Hello Games has shown us so far: the execution and delivery is terrible.

[h1]Retried with a new save game[/h1]
Got a new planet, and a much better start. My previous points are still valid though.
At most, Survival seems to slow your progress, making the game even more slow and tedious than it already was.

Apart from some performance improvements, I see absolutely NO improvements to the overal gameplay or the many, many complaints about odd design choices.

1) Milestones still interrupt gameplay, and this is really bad during survival.
2) Creatures are still way too stupid to be called 'life'.
3) Inventory management is still crap
4) It's still holding a button to do shit, but they even removed the 'hold the button and mouse over all discoveries to mass upload', making you upload everything 1 at a time!
5) Not too sure about this one, but planets still don't seem to rotate (watched a distant planet for a quarter sol, didn't move at all).

The few changes that I can (sort of) appreciate are these:

1) Life Support energy is more dynamic; running and using jetpack have larger impacts on your life support, while standing still doesn't use any life support energy.
2) Need certain tech to mine certain minerals (although this just slows progression further).
3) Yeah, I got nothing else...

Reviews.216184:
Almost exactly five years later, No Man's Sky is nothing like it was on launch. Is it better? Sort of.

I'm giving this game a thumbs up because regardless of my feelings on it, I would recommend it IF you are a fan of Subnautica-ish survival building and resource management games. It has an enormous amount of content and an active developer with good community engagement. Base building is robust and the tech ladder is at least somewhat interesting. Planetary variety has continually increased since launch and I see no reason to doubt that such trends will continue. If you buy NMS as a survival building game in 2021 you will probably get your money's worth in time and enjoyment.

Be aware though that NMS is a slower game than you likely will anticipate. The notoriously sluggish UI and limited early-game mobility encourage a more laid-back approach to progress, which sets the standard for a lot of the remainder of this game's content. Don't come into NMS with the intent to rush through its tech trees and content. Be patient with it and it'll be more fun.

For me, NMS is at its best, ironically, when you're alone. The music, visuals and general presentation are most immersive when you're wandering about a desolate planet in first person with nobody else around. This is also why, for me at least, this game's most persistent flaw is in how hilariously overpopulated with NPCs  every system is. I do wish it would be at least closer to 50/50 dead systems and populous ones. Updates have made this problem far worse - a greater emphasis on multiplayer, base sharing and social events has pushed the game further and further from the very slow and solitary enjoyment I normally get from it. 

The biggest flaw that no longer exists from launch is the shallow economy. Originally, NMS had so hilariously few practical options for making money that I spent nearly fifty hours just wandering around, grabbing Gravitino Balls and selling them at stations with a high margin. The introduction of a far more robust economy, artifacts with high unit yield, other routes like scanning & farming, etc etc... have made the game drastically more interesting to grind through.

This is made even better by the inclusion of many more late-game goals to grind for. Instead of just searching for a good-looking 48-slot ship, you've now got ship classes, freighters and very extensive upgrade trees to wander through. While the onboarding & tutorial for it is far worse, the new crafting system has far more depth and purpose than stumbling from building to building, trying to randomly pull the recipe you wanted like a Gacha game. 

All of this is great, but I find it at odds with what I originally enjoyed from this game. Call me a moron, but I actually prefer the release build of NMS if only because the strange, barren nature of its original gameplay loop was better suited to the general feeling the game gave off. It feels a little faker, a little less "itself" - for lack of a better word - like it's spent the last five years compromising on the original vision to appease the angry players from the early days. I would have much preferred they kept the wayward weirdness and just spent the last half-decade improving the planetary generation, but for a $60 game you gotta appease to normal sensibilities somehow. 

As an aside, the story has gotten continually more convoluted and pretentious with every major update and I love it for that. It's so over-wordy and overblown for the generally stakes-less content and low-intensity tasks it puts you through - to a point that every time a console waxes poetic about the Natures of Things it's hard not to laugh. It's really really high-concept simulation sci-fi and while I don't think it really sticks the landing, it does have a lot of neat ideas and plenty of idle reading to do when you're bored. 

TL;DR - While I don't really think NMS has grown into the hole it left in everyone's expectations from half a decade earlier, it is certainly a decent game now, with more than enough content to justify the price tag. Pick it up if you know what you're getting into.
